notes: High overlap (6 shared claims: C91-C96) about vm2 muscle fate specificity. LLM finds evidence comprehensive enough to rule out general fate defects. Peer reviewers explicitly request additional fate markers and morphological analysis, stating current evidence is insufficient to resolve whether Notch absence causes partial fate switch or selective disruption of muscle arm program.

Strong overlap (11 shared claims: C2, C28-C30, C32-C38) on Notch-Delta pathway components and mechanisms. Both agree the core mechanistic findings about APX-1, LIN-12, SEL-12 and their cell-autonomous/non-autonomous functions are well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge this documents an interesting muscle differentiation program controlled by Notch.

Perfect match (3 shared claims: C26, C27, C98) on temporal aspects of LIN-12 function. Both agree on the differential sensitivity model and late L4 requirement for muscle arm development, independent from earlier vulval roles. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these temporal findings as part of the developmental program documentation.

Good overlap (4 shared claims: C9-C11, C73) on independence of muscle arm development from neurons. Both agree that genetic ablation and synaptic transport mutant data demonstrate autonomous postsynaptic development. Peer reviewers accept this as documenting a muscle differentiation program that precedes postsynaptic differentiation.

Strong overlap (9 shared claims: C48-C54, C104-C105) on UNC-40 and MADD-2 regulation by Notch. Both accept the molecular findings about downstream effectors and their LIN-12-dependent regulation. Peer reviewers implicitly support these as part of the accepted developmental program for muscle arm formation.

Moderate overlap (5 shared claims: C18-C22) on functional importance demonstrated by egg-laying defects and calcium imaging. Both accept the phenotypic characterization showing behavioral consequences of muscle arm absence. Peer reviewers acknowledge these observations document the muscle arm phenotype.

Limited overlap (5 shared claims: C47, C63-C66) on UNC-40/MADD-2 genetic interactions. LLM R4 focuses on their functional relationship while peer R3 covers broader UNC-40/MADD-2 regulation. Both support their respective claim sets, but address partially different aspects of the same molecular system.

Limited overlap (4 shared claims: C57-C60) on ectopic UNC-40 sufficiency. LLM R3 focuses specifically on sufficiency experiments while peer R3 covers broader UNC-40/MADD-2 findings. Both support the overlapping claims about UNC-40's role in muscle arm formation.

Minimal overlap (2 shared claims: C70-C71) on temporal independence of pre/postsynaptic development. LLM R12 focuses on this specific aspect while peer R6 covers broader independence claims including neuronal requirements. Both support the temporal independence findings.

Minimal overlap (3 shared claims: C15-C17) on specific allele characterization. LLM R1 covers comprehensive Notch pathway evidence while peer R4 focuses on phenotypic characterization. Both support the overlapping claims about mutant phenotypes.

Fundamental disagreement on interpretation. LLM R1 finds Notch pathway requirement for vm2 target selection well-supported (C1 shared, plus C13-C17, C28-C30, C32-C38). Peer R1 explicitly challenges synapse specificity interpretation (C1, C6, C23, C69, C108-C110), stating data do not address synaptic function and requesting substantial revision to focus on muscle arm formation rather than synaptic specificity claims.

LLM R8 addresses organizational role of vulval epithelial cells (C12, C31, C74-C79). No corresponding peer review result directly addresses these claims. Peer reviewers do not challenge the guidepost cell model but focus critique elsewhere.

LLM R9 addresses positive feedback model via LAG-1 binding sites (C39-C42). No corresponding peer review result directly addresses these autoregulation claims. Peer reviewers do not explicitly challenge this molecular mechanism.

LLM R10 addresses novel UNC-40 ligand speculation (C99-C103). No corresponding peer review result addresses these claims. LLM already rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature; peer reviewers do not comment on ligand identity questions.

Peer R1 includes claims C6, C108-C110 about synapse specificity that are not grouped in any LLM result as standalone claims (though C6 may be implicit in other groupings). Peer reviewers explicitly reject synapse specificity interpretation as overreach beyond the data.
